title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addresses the International Space Summit in Paris, France
subtitle:
The promise of space is infinite, and our responsibility is collective: PM

Our choices must be clear, cooperation over confrontation, sustainability over short-term gain, and inclusion over exclusion: PM

We support a safe, secure, peaceful and sustainable space domain, anchored in international law, dialogue and multilateral cooperation: PM

ISRO, which stands at the heart of this journey, has earned global admiration for its excellence and cost-effective missions: PM

Let the Space Summit in Paris send a clear message: we will explore together, innovate together and protect space together, for all humanity, and for generations to come: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today addressed the International Space Summit held in Paris, France, via Video conference. The Prime Minister thanked President Emmanuel Macron for taking a timely initiative and extending a gracious invitation. He expressed delight in participating in this landmark gathering. "I am happy to be a part of the first International Space Summit," remarked Shri Modi.
Reflecting on humanity's enduring fascination with the cosmos, the Prime Minister observed that space has inspired human imagination for centuries. He highlighted that this frontier now shapes everyday life on Earth, from climate and crops to oceans and communities. "The promise of space is infinite, and our responsibility is collective," noted Shri Modi.
Addressing the growing complexity of the cosmic environment, the Prime Minister emphasized that orbits are becoming more crowded, technologies more powerful, and actors more numerous. He stressed that global partnerships must prioritize long-term sustainability over short-term gains. "Our choices must be clear: cooperation over confrontation, sustainability over short-term gain, and inclusion over exclusion," asserted Shri Modi.
Connecting India's philosophical worldview to outer space, the Prime Minister pointed out that the nation's approach is firmly rooted in the ethos of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, meaning One Earth, One Family, One Future. He advocated for this unifying spirit to travel beyond our planet to ensure a secure domain. "We support a safe, secure, peaceful and sustainable space domain, anchored in international law, dialogue and multilateral cooperation," affirmed Shri Modi.
Highlighting the importance of transparent research, the Prime Minister stressed that India's cosmic journey perfectly reflects the philosophy of universal welfare. He noted that the ethical sharing of information is paramount for global progress. "Scientific data must serve the common good, with openness and integrity," observed Shri Modi.
Tracing the remarkable trajectory of the nation's aerospace enterprise, the Prime Minister highlighted the practical benefits of satellite technology for weather forecasting, disaster management, and navigation. He noted that these advanced capabilities directly serve grassroots communities, including farmers and fishermen. "ISRO, which stands at the heart of this journey, has earned global admiration for its excellence and cost-effective missions," remarked Shri Modi.
Detailing India's collaborative international footprint in launch services, the Prime Minister highlighted the successful deployment of more than 430 payloads from 34 countries aboard domestic rockets. He emphasized the broad global utility of these cooperative scientific endeavors. "ISRO’s technologies and partnerships serve not only India, but the wider world," noted Shri Modi.
Ascribing this institutional success to the relentless human capital of the nation, the Prime Minister paid tribute to the dedication and hard work of generations of Indian scientists, engineers, and technicians. He commended how their tireless efforts have secured a place of pride among spacefaring nations. "Working day and night, they have built ISRO’s global reputation mission by mission, success by success," affirmed Shri Modi.
Recalling monumental milestones in planetary science, the Prime Minister cited that Aditya-L1 is currently unlocking the secrets of the Sun, while an Indian astronaut visited the International Space Station last year. He proudly recounted the historic lunar touchdown that set a new global benchmark. "Chandrayaan-3 made India the first nation to land near the lunar south pole," noted Shri Modi.
Outlining ambitious futuristic targets for the national roadmap, the Prime Minister announced plans to establish an indigenous space station by 2035 and send an astronaut to the Moon by 2040. He maintained that these long-term efforts are driven by a singular, overarching purpose. "In all these efforts, our guiding principle has been clear: their benefits must reach all humanity," asserted Shri Modi.
Describing the rapid evolution of the domestic commercial ecosystem, the Prime Minister observed that India's private space sector is surging in a big way alongside institutional agencies. He acknowledged the dynamic synergy forming between emerging startups and established organizations. "The energy of enterprise is joining the excellence of ISRO," remarked Shri Modi.
Valuing long-standing bilateral relations, the Prime Minister recalled that France has been a trusted partner since the inception of the Indian space program at Thumba in the 1960s. He emphasized that current joint initiatives successfully merge high-level research with tangible societal benefits. "Today, our cooperation spans Earth observation and advanced technologies, uniting scientific excellence with human purpose," affirmed Shri Modi.
Extending an open invitation to international stakeholders, the Prime Minister called upon the global community to participate in upcoming exploratory missions. He welcomed worldwide partners to join hands in pioneering the next wave of cosmic discovery. "We invite France and the world to be co-travellers in India’s next space frontier," remarked Shri Modi.
Concluding his video address, the Prime Minister conveyed his best wishes to all the distinguished participants of the summit. He urged the international community to safeguard the celestial environment through collaborative exploration and innovation. "Let the Space Summit in Paris send a clear message: we will explore together, innovate together and protect space together, for all humanity, and for generations to come," asserted Shri Modi.

title: Drylands Can Become a Great Strength with Right Science, Policy and Market Support: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
subtitle:
Transforming Drylands Requires a Whole-of-System, Whole-of-Society and Whole-of-Government Approach: Secretary DARE

Dryland Congress 2026 Opens in New Delhi: Breeding, Climate Resilience and Nutrition Take Centre Stage on Day One
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 9:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today called for an integrated approach based on science, policy and market support to transform dryland agriculture, strengthen food and nutritional security and improve farmers’ livelihoods. Addressing the Opening Session of Dryland Congress 2026 at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi, Shri Chouhan said that drylands should not be viewed as a weakness and, with appropriate scientific interventions, policies and market support, can become a source of strength for India and other regions facing similar challenges.
Dryland Congress 2026, being held in New Delhi from 10 September 2026, has brought together more than 800 delegates from over 25 countries, including scientists, policymakers, development partners, industry representatives, academicians, civil society organisations and farmers, to deliberate on science-, technology- and policy-based solutions for resilient and sustainable dryland agriculture. The three-day Congress focuses on strengthening crop resilience, sustainable management of dryland landscapes, nutrition, markets and policies, while improving livelihood opportunities for communities dependent on dryland agriculture.
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan emphasised that food security, nutritional security and farmers’ prosperity must remain at the centre of efforts to transform agricultural systems. He said that the ultimate measure of success should not be increased production alone, but also improved livelihoods and prosperity of farming communities. He stated, “Drylands are not a weakness. With the right science, the right policy and the right market support, they can become one of the greatest strengths for India, Africa and other regions facing similar challenges.”
The Opening Session was presided over by Dr R. S. Paroda, Former Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Former Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). Former leaders of ICAR and ICRISAT, including Dr Panjab Singh, Dr Trilochan Mohapatra and Dr William D. Dar, participated in the session along with Ms Cathy Reade, Board Chair, ICRISAT, and Dr Sandra Milach, Chief Scientist, CGIAR. Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, and Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT, are the Patrons of the Congress. The Congress Co-Chairs are Dr Stanford Blade, Deputy Director General – Research and Innovation, ICRISAT; Dr Devendra Kumar Yadava, Deputy Director General – Crop Science, ICAR; and Shri Sanjay Agarwal, Additional Director General, ICRISAT.
The farmer perspective was represented by Padma Shri awardee and farmer Bhikiya Ladakya Dhinda, underlining the importance of incorporating farmers’ experiences and requirements in strategies for transforming dryland agriculture.
During the Opening Session, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan also launched Transforming the Drylands: The ICRISAT Journey, edited by Dr Himanshu Pathak and Dr Stanford Blade and published by ICRISAT. The publication documents more than five decades of ICRISAT’s work in science, innovation, partnerships and impact across Asia, Africa and other regions. The Dryland Congress 2026 Abstract Book, containing more than 250 abstracts, and the ICRISAT Research and Corporate Profile, highlighting the institute’s work across Accelerated Crop Improvement, Resilient Farming Systems and Transforming Agri-Food Systems, were also launched.
The technical programme on the first day featured three thematic sessions — “Breeding for Tomorrow: Accelerating Genetic Gains”, “Climate-Resilient Dryland Landscapes” and “Better Diets and Nutrition through Markets & Policies”. The sessions brought together experts to deliberate on accelerating genetic gains in crops, strengthening climate resilience, improving management of dryland landscapes, enhancing nutrition and creating better livelihood opportunities.
Dr M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR, delivered a visionary address on India’s experience in transforming agricultural systems and the lessons emerging for the Global South. He emphasised that transforming drylands requires interventions beyond agriculture and called for a whole-of-system, whole-of-society and whole-of-government approach to create opportunities and improve livelihoods in dryland regions. He said, “From recommendations to action, from silos to systems — that is the pathway to transforming dryland agriculture.”
Shri Narendra Bhooshan, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Government of India, spoke on reimagining drylands through digital public infrastructure, land resources management and community action. His address highlighted the role of integrated approaches in strengthening land and resource management and supporting communities in dryland regions.
Dr Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT, highlighted the global importance of drylands for food systems and livelihoods and called for a roadmap to make drylands productive, profitable and resilient while creating livelihood opportunities and reducing out-migration. He emphasised the need to make drylands central to future agricultural development.
Dr R. S. Paroda stressed the importance of water management in dryland agriculture and called for ensuring greater economic and nutritional value from every drop of water. Dr Panjab Singh emphasised that the next phase of dryland development should focus on farming systems that are profitable, resilient, environmentally sustainable and attractive to future generations.
Dr Trilochan Mohapatra highlighted the importance of South-South cooperation in sharing knowledge, expertise and successful models to accelerate the adoption and scaling of solutions across dryland regions. Ms Cathy Reade, Board Chair, ICRISAT, called for greater global focus, investment and action in dryland agriculture and highlighted the potential of South-South cooperation in strengthening resilience across dryland landscapes.
Dr William D. Dar, Former Director General, ICRISAT, emphasised that South-South cooperation enables countries of the Global South to learn, innovate and scale solutions together as equal partners. Dr Sandra Milach, Chief Scientist, CGIAR, noted that India is increasingly emerging as a source of solutions for the Global South, with innovations that can be adapted and scaled across dryland regions facing similar challenges.
The Dryland Congress 2026 will continue its deliberations over the next two days, focusing on scientific innovation, climate resilience, sustainable farming systems, nutrition, markets, policies and livelihood opportunities to support the transformation of dryland agriculture.

title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Engages Farmer Leaders Nationwide on Proposed Stronger Seed Act
subtitle:
Government Committed to Shaping Every Farm Policy Through Dialogue and Consultation with Farmers: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

1966 Law No Longer Meets Today’s Challenges; 70% of Seeds Outside Its Scope, Strong Action Against Fake Seeds Essential: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Farmers’ Rights Fully Protected; No Restrictions on Traditional and Farmers’ Seed Varieties: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Heavy Fines and Jail Terms Proposed to Crack Down on Fake Seed Trade: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Mandatory Registration and QR Codes to Ensure End-to-End Traceability of Seeds: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

States to Get Powers to Release New Seed Varieties Faster: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

Compensation for Farmers Within 15 Days; Seed Security Fund Proposed in Every State: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government is working on a stronger Seed Act to protect farmers from fake and substandard seeds. Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today held a consultation with leaders of farmer organisations from across the country at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi. Representatives from almost all states participated in the consultation and shared their experiences and suggestions on the proposed legislation. Around 20 farmer organisations submitted their views during the meeting. Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra and senior officials were also present.
Representatives of the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, various factions of the Bharatiya Kisan Union, All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC), Kisan Mahapanchayat, Bharatiya Krishak Samaj, Gaon Kisan Unnayan, Society for Independent Farmers Association (SIFA), Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, Telangana Rythu Sangham, Maharashtra’s Shetkari organisations, Gujarat’s Khedut Samaj, National Kisan Progressive Association from Rajasthan and Bihar, Tamil Nadu’s Vivasayigal Sangam, Jharkhand’s Pragatisheel Krishi Manch and a farmers’ organisation from Kottayam, Kerala, among others, participated in the consultation.
Existing 1966 law needs to be updated
Shri Chouhan said the existing Seed Act was enacted in 1966 and the Seeds Control Order came into force in 1983. With significant changes in agriculture over the past six decades, the existing framework is no longer adequate to address emerging challenges, including the entry of fake and poor-quality seeds into the market and gaps in fixing responsibility. He said farmers had raised the need for new Seed and Pesticide Acts during the Viksit Krishi Sankalp Abhiyan. The government had invited suggestions on the draft Seed Act in November-December 2025 and received around 18,000 suggestions from farmers and farmer organisations. The consultation process has now been resumed to seek direct inputs from organisations working closely with farmers. Shri Chouhan said there would be no haste in finalising the law and no deadline has been fixed. Suggestions from farmers, farmer organisations and other stakeholders will continue to be considered before the government moves ahead.
70% of seeds outside existing law’s ambit
Shri Chouhan said around 70% of seeds currently fall outside the ambit of the existing Seed Act, while seed-related procedures differ across states and the existing penalty provisions are inadequate. He said the new legislation is therefore necessary to establish a stronger, more effective and uniform regulatory framework against fake and substandard seeds.
Farmers’ traditional seed rights to remain protected
The Minister made it clear that the proposed law will not restrict farmers’ existing rights. Farmers will continue to be free to use, exchange and sell traditional and farmers’ varieties of seeds. Registration will not be mandatory for traditional seeds. Farmers may voluntarily register their varieties if they wish to do so. A farmer producing seed for personal use, for distribution within the village or even for a company will not be required to undertake digital registration under these provisions.
Up to ₹30 lakh penalty and imprisonment for serious offences
The proposed law classifies offences into three categories:
Minor violations: Warning for the first offence and a penalty of up to ₹50,000 for the second offence.
Deliberate violations: For offences such as failure to affix a QR code, failure to provide required data or incorrect branding, the penalty will be ₹1 lakh for the first offence and ₹2 lakh for the second.
Serious offences: Selling fake seeds, conducting business without registration or deliberate fraud will attract a penalty of up to ₹30 lakh along with imprisonment.
Shri Chouhan said the stringent provisions will act as a strong deterrent against those involved in the illegal seed trade.
100% registration and QR-based traceability
Under the proposed legislation, all seeds and planting material will have to be registered in a national register. Unregistered seeds will be illegal and cannot be sold in the market. Every seed packet will carry a QR code, enabling farmers to trace its origin, manufacturer, laboratory clearance and movement through the supply chain. Shri Chouhan said the absence of an effective traceability system currently makes it difficult to fix responsibility when seeds fail. The new law will make traceability mandatory and establish a structured system for identifying responsibility.
States to get greater powers to release new varieties
The proposed law will empower state governments to release new seed varieties on the recommendation of state-level committees, while national standards will remain applicable. This will enable states to release varieties suited to their local climate and regional requirements more efficiently. All varieties will be recorded in a single national online register, accessible to both the Centre and states, avoiding duplication.
Seed Security Fund and compensation within 15 days
Responding to farmers’ demands, the proposed law provides for a Seed Security Fund in every state, to be managed by the respective state governments. Penalties and recoveries collected under the Seed Act will be deposited into these funds. In case of seed failure or loss to a farmer, a verification committee will ensure compensation within 15 days. Farmers will also retain the right to seek compensation under the Consumer Protection Act.
Farmer consultations to continue
Shri Chouhan thanked farmer organisation leaders for sharing their experiences and suggestions and said all inputs would be examined seriously. Suggestions found feasible will be considered for incorporation into the final draft. He reiterated that the government under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is committed to framing policies through consultation and dialogue with farmers, with their interests at the centre of the process. The Minister said the ongoing consultation is an important step towards protecting Indian farmers from fake and substandard seeds and creating a stronger, more accountable seed regulatory system. He added that consultations with other stakeholders are also being held, with farmers remaining central to the process. Shri Chouhan said the proposed legislation is part of the effort to realise Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of prosperous, empowered and self-reliant farmers.

Tiu Laurel, Secretary, Department of Agriculture, The Philippines, representing the Chair of the ASEAN Ministers on Agriculture and Forestry, and H.E. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan,Minister, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, India, representing the Republic of India.
The Meeting reaffirmed the importance of ASEAN-India cooperation in food, agriculture and forestry as a practical and mutually beneficial component of the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The Meeting underscored its commitment to advancing cooperation that supports food security and nutrition, farmers' livelihoods, sustainable and low emission development, innovation, research and development, rural prosperity and the resilience of agriculture and forest systems.
The Meeting welcomed ASEAN 2045: Our Shared Future and the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 for a Resilient, Innovative, Dynamic and People-Centred ASEAN. The Meeting also welcomed the ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on the Vision for Food, Agriculture and Forestry Towards 2045 and the ASEAN Food, Agriculture and Forestry Sectoral Plan 2026-2030, which provide strategic direction for a sustainable, inclusive, resilient and secure sector that nurtures farmers' livelihoods, safeguards the environment, fosters innovation and contributes to climate change adaptation and mitigation.
The Meeting exchanged views on the implications of global uncertainties for food, agriculture and forestry, including climate change and extreme weather events, geopolitical and economic tensions, volatility in energy, fertiliser and agricultural input markets, disruptions to trade and logistics, and plant and animal health, transboundary plant pests and animal diseases. The Meeting emphasised the importance of maintaining and ensuring the flow of food and essential agricultural input supply chains (fertilizers, seeds, and pesticides), strengthening regional monitoring and early warning, diversifying sources of supply, and supporting smallholders and vulnerable groups. The Meeting agreed that ASEAN and India should deepen practical cooperation to build resilient, sustainable and responsive food and agricultural systems.
The Meeting commended the progress made in implementing the ASEAN-India Medium-Term Plan of Action for Cooperation in Agriculture and Forestry 2021-2025. During this period, ASEAN and India sustained ministerial and senior-official policy dialogue and strengthened cooperation on food security, climate-resilient and sustainable agriculture, conservation and nature-positive approaches, sustainable soil management, human-resource development, digitalisation, science and technology, and exchanges among institutions and farmers.
The Meeting highlighted several notable achievements under the 2021-2025 cooperation period. These included the ASEAN-India Joint Leaders' Statement on Strengthening Food Security and Nutrition in Response to Crises; the ASEAN-India Millets Festivals held in Jakarta and New Delhi in 2023, which promoted dietary diversification, nutrition and climate-resilient crops; and the launch in 2024 of the ASEAN-India Fellowship for Higher Education in Agriculture and Allied Sciences, providing for 50 Master's fellowships over five years for students from ASEAN Member States. The Meeting also noted progress in advancing cooperative initiatives on smart farming and soil health, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things and machine learning for precision agriculture, and farmer-to-farmer knowledge exchange.
The implementation of cooperation areas should strengthen linkages among research, innovation, technology transfer, advisory and agricultural extension services, the private sector, and farmers’ organizations, with a view to narrowing the gap between technology development and practical application and facilitating the scaling-up of technologies in agricultural production.
Building on these achievements and the new strategic direction of ASEAN, the Meeting looked forward to adoption and implementation of the ASEAN-India Medium-Term Plan of Action for Cooperation in Agriculture and Forestry 2026-2030. The new Plan will guide cooperation in four mutually reinforcing areas: policy dialogue, food security, trade, investment and resilient value chains; institutional networking, information exchange and digital innovation; capacity building, technology cooperation and joint research and development; and human-resource development, farmer exchanges and inclusive rural enterprise.
The Meeting agreed that implementation of the new Plan should prioritise practical, scalable and farmer-centred initiatives. These may include cooperation on low-emission rice and water productivity; digital agriculture and forestry, including the application of artificial intelligence, Internet of Things and other emerging digital technologies; soil health and bio-inputs; climate-resilient and nutritious crops; food safety; postharvest management and reduction of food loss and waste; alternatives to open crop-residue burning and circular bioeconomy solutions; resilient food supply chains and agricultural inputs; sustainable forest management, forest and landscape restoration, agroforestry, forest monitoring and responsible forest-based value chains and community enterprises.
The Meeting encouraged the participation of research and education institutions, farmers' organisations, cooperatives, micro, small and medium enterprises, the private sector, financial institutions and relevant development partners, as appropriate.
The Meeting agreed to strengthen market connectivity and access; promote cooperation in value-added processing, preservation technologies, and post-harvest management to enhance the quality and value addition of agricultural products; and enhance connectivity in agricultural and forestry logistics to facilitate the movement and distribution of agricultural and forestry products.
The Meeting tasked the relevant senior officials and working mechanisms of ASEAN and India to translate the Plan into a results-oriented rolling work programme with clear priorities, lead agencies, expected outputs, timelines and possible sources of support. The Meeting encouraged the effective mobilisation of available ASEAN-India funding mechanisms, voluntary national resources and other mutually agreed support, subject to applicable rules and procedures. Progress will be regularly monitored, with a view to ensuring timely implementation, measurable benefits and the scaling-up of successful initiatives.
The Meeting agreed to convene the Tenth ASEAN-India Ministerial Meeting on Agriculture and Forestry in 2028.
The Meeting expressed its sincere appreciation to the Government of India for the warm hospitality and excellent arrangements made for the 9th AIMMAF Meeting.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Accelerating India-Russia Economic Partnership to Achieve $100 Billion Bilateral Trade by 2030
subtitle:
Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights Opportunities to Expand India’s Exports to Russia Across Pharmaceuticals, Auto Components and Food Products

Shri Goyal Invites Russian Businesses to Utilize India’s Plug-and-Play Industrial Corridors to Manufacture in India
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today called for an accelerated India-Russia economic and industrial partnership, urging businesses from both countries to work towards achieving the target of $100 billion in bilateral trade and $50 billion in two-way investment by 2030. Addressing the INNOPROM India 2026 Co-Chair Plenary Session with Russian Minister of Industry and Trade Mr. Anton Alikhanov in New Delhi, Shri Goyal said that the targets set by the two Heads of State would be a measure of the performance of both governments and businesses.
Shri Goyal said that increasing bilateral trade from the current base of around $60 billion to $100 billion would require adding about $40 billion in the next four years and sustained double-digit growth year-on-year. He stressed that achieving this would require significant efforts not only from the governments but equally from businesses in both countries.
Highlighting the opportunities for diversifying bilateral trade, Shri Goyal said that Indian exports of meat and edible meat products had more than doubled from $36 million to $97 million, an increase of nearly 170 per cent. Fish and aquatic products grew from $123 million to $159 million, an increase of nearly 30 per cent, while exports of edible vegetables rose from $38 million to $54 million, an increase of 40 per cent. Exports of coffee, tea and spices increased by 13 per cent to $116 million, while products of the milling industry had nearly doubled.
Shri Goyal said these figures reflected growing demand in the Russian market for products from Indian farmers, food processors, micro, small and medium enterprises and MSME exporters. He noted that only a small portion of the potential had been tapped so far. Referring to the complementarity between the two economies, he said there were several products where Russia is a significant importer and India is a significant exporter globally, but India is not yet a significant exporter to Russia. He identified pharmaceuticals, auto components, tractors and food products among the opportunities waiting to be explored.
The Minister said that non-energy trade between the two countries remained much smaller than its potential and represented the headroom that needed to be filled to move bilateral trade from $60 billion to $100 billion. He said rebalancing bilateral trade through greater Indian exports of pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, textiles, food products, marine products and auto products would be central to achieving the target.
On investment, Shri Goyal said that the India-Russia priority investment projects mechanism is currently tracking 40 live investment projects across advanced manufacturing, energy, mining, railways and emerging technologies. He called upon the Russian side to help open the doors wider for Indian investments in Russia in pharmaceuticals, IT, artificial intelligence, services, engineering and railways, so that the $50 billion investment target becomes genuinely a two-way street.
Shri Goyal said India and Russia are fast-tracking a new bilateral investment treaty to provide investors on both sides with the legal certainty they seek while finalising investment destinations. He also said that India and the Eurasian Economic Union, comprising Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Armenia and the Kyrgyz Republic, had launched formal free trade negotiations last year and that India was committed to concluding them early, opening new markets for industries and, importantly, MSMEs.
The Minister said that the two countries continue to strengthen national and local currency settlement mechanisms, noting that payment friction, more often than tariffs, slows trade on the ground. He also highlighted investments in the physical backbone of the bilateral relationship, including the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chennai-Vladivostok maritime corridor, stressing that connectivity is a part of trade policy and not merely infrastructure.
Shri Goyal outlined five specific asks for businesses and officials of both countries. First, he urged businesses to finalise at least one deal before leaving Delhi, identify one new friend and partner, and take forward at least one concrete project. Second, he called upon businesses to add a new non-energy line to their trade and investment plans, particularly in pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, chemicals, auto components, tractor parts, textiles, food, agri-tech and marine products, stating that these sectors would help achieve the $100 billion bilateral trade target.
Third, Shri Goyal called upon Russian industry to manufacture in India and not only sell in the country. He said India's national industrial corridors are investment-ready, with plug-and-play infrastructure available for global partners. He highlighted India's youthful talent and skilled labour as an important resource for Russian companies, noting that such skilled labour may be difficult to find in Russia.
Fourth, he urged Indian industry to go to Russia not merely as visitors but as investors and exporters, and to cultivate friendships, new partnerships and new business potential.
Fifth, Shri Goyal called upon officials on both sides to listen to industry and identify the factors that are blocking trade and investment. He asked them to examine whether payment systems, certification requirements, standards, logistics, visa access or approvals were creating difficulties. He assured the Russian side that he and his colleagues stood ready to help make the entire journey seamless, smooth and exciting.
Highlighting India's strengths as an investment and manufacturing destination, Shri Goyal said India offers scale and a rapidly expanding industrial manufacturing base under initiatives including Make in India, Digital India, the industrial park scheme and Startup India. He said India invests $130 billion every year in creating new infrastructure and strengthening its capacity in airports, ports, expressways, railways, inland waterways, power infrastructure, water infrastructure and industrial parks. He said there is a strong drive to create the right ecosystem and infrastructure to host global partners in India.
Shri Goyal said India provides talent and skills in abundance, along with a young and aspirational population willing to innovate, design and co-design, co-create and co-manufacture with its global partners. He said Russia brings decades of engineering excellence, particularly in aerospace, metallurgy, nuclear technology and mining. He emphasised that when the strengths of India and Russia come together, the relationship can go beyond trade and build resilience into both economies.
Referring to the longstanding India-Russia relationship, Shri Goyal said it had weathered seven decades of a changing world. He said the task before the two countries now was not merely continuity but acceleration. Quoting Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said, “The greatest strength of India-Russia relations lies in trust. This trust provides both direction and momentum to our joint efforts and serves as the launchpad inspiring new dreams and aspirations.”
Shri Goyal said the presence of INNOPROM in India for the first time in its history was significant. He noted that for over a decade, INNOPROM, the Global Industrial Technology Exhibition, had served as a platform where Russian engineering and manufacturing presented themselves to the world. He said bringing the platform to India demonstrated where the two nations now stand and reflected their readiness to move “from protocols to production, from intent to industry.”
Shri Goyal said the two ministries had been working closely over the past several months to deepen economic and industrial cooperation and expressed confidence that the visit of Russian Minister of Industry and Trade Mr. Anton Alikhanov would accelerate this progress.
Concluding his address, Shri Goyal thanked Minister Alikhanov and the entire Russian delegation for their partnership and wished INNOPROM India 2026 and all businesses represented at the exhibition a productive final stretch.

title: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia Calls For Inclusive and Trusted Intelligent Finance at the Global Fintech Festival 2026
subtitle:
Union Minister of Communications Hails India As The Data Capital Of The World

Broadband access grew from 6 crore to 103 crore in a decade, a 16x jump: Shri Scindia

Rolled out in 2022, India's 5G now covers 99.9% districts and 85% population in 26 months, with capex of Rs 4.5 lakh crore: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia

Smartphones are the new ‘bank branch’ for Indians: Union Minister of Communications
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 10:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, called for an inclusive and trusted digital financial ecosystem, emphasising that before finance becomes intelligent, it must become inclusive. Speaking at the Global Fintech Festival 2026 in Mumbai, he said the telecom network, an invisible highway that cannot be seen, is the very foundation on which fintech evolves. Together with compute and trust, connectivity forms the new digital trinity powering the next phase of digital finance.
Highlighting the scale of India’s digital transformation, Shri Scindia said that around 25 crore people had access to the internet a decade ago, compared to 100 crore today. Broadband access has grown from just 6 crore to 103 crore, representing nearly 16 times growth in 10 years. He emphasised that technology must become ubiquitous, across India and the world.
The Union Minister said that smartphones have become bank branches, taking citizens from internet connectivity to credit and investment. With around 6.5 lakh villages becoming participants in the digital economy, he said every connected village can become a member of the global fintech ecosystem.
Highlighting India’s rapid 5G expansion, Shri Scindia said that following the launch of 5G in 2022, India achieved capability across 99.9% of districts, covering almost 85% of the population, within 26 months. Shri Scindia also noted that the rollout has been supported by over 5 lakh 5G base stations.
Furthermore, the Union Minister highlighted the sharp reduction in the cost of communications, noting that data costs have fallen to around 10 cents per GB. He said India has become the world’s cheapest data capital, making digital technology increasingly accessible.
Shri Scindia highlighted the journey of UPI, which began with around 90,000 transactions in its first month and has today scaled to more than 740 banks. UPI has processed around 24,162 crore transactions in FY 2025–26, worth approximately ₹314 lakh crore, demonstrating the scale that India’s Digital Public Infrastructure can achieve.
The Union Minister of Communications noted that 84% of domestic digital transactions take place on UPI, while India accounts for approximately 49% of the world’s real-time digital payment volumes. He credited the fintech ecosystem for this achievement and said that India’s success demonstrates the power of technology built at scale.
Union Minister Shri Scindia highlighted the success of UPI as an expression of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. He said the technology is being taken to nine countries at no cost to them, while the world is looking towards taking this model to the next 20 countries.
Additionally, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said the architecture of digital finance rests on networks that carry connections, trust and interoperable platforms that connect institutions. He underlined three principles: innovation scales when infrastructure is open; inclusion scales when infrastructure is affordable; and trust scales when infrastructure is secure.
Highlighting the role of Jan Dhan accounts and DigiLocker, the Union Minister said around 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts and 9 billion documents on DigiLocker have dramatically reduced the distance between citizens and their ability to access finance. He emphasised that finance no longer needs to depend on the physical presence of a bank branch. “The smartphone is the bank branch,” he said, noting that a smartphone can take fintech to every citizen.
Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia highlighted that fintech connectivity has reached almost every village in the North Eastern Region, driven by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s impetus and sankalp. Through Digital Bharat Nidhi, around 22,000 towers are being established across 34,000 villages without telecom connectivity, with the objective of ensuring 100% saturation.
Shri Scindia said that as India works towards 100% saturation on the mobile front, a new arterial system is being established, extending from mobile to terrestrial networks. He highlighted the role of Gram Panchayats in creating first-mile, middle-mile and last-mile connectivity to reach the remaining villages.
The Union Minister also highlighted the national AI capabilities and compute power converge with digital infrastructure, AI can personalise financial advice and credit and increasingly make financial services autonomous.
Shri Scindia emphasised that with greater intelligence comes greater responsibility. He called for financial systems to be ring-fenced, with strong firewalls and safeguards to protect citizens and their financial security.
Sanchar Saathi, a Government of India initiative that protects citizens against suspicious connections and enables stolen devices to be blocked. Shri Scindia highlighted the AI powered tool- ASTR, which has helped disconnect more than 88 lakh suspicious mobile connections.
The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator ring-fences suspicious transactions and helps stop fraudulent payments before money leaves citizens’ accounts. He called for SOPs across banking networks to strengthen the protection of citizens and their financial capabilities.
Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia emphasised the need to shift from detecting fraud after it happens to preventing it before it occurs. He said the objective must be to move from reactive security to predictive trust.
The Union Minister called for the creation of a Trust Grid for finance, bringing together telecom, digital identity, UPI and financial systems. He said greater convergence of Aadhaar and UPI can give every citizen the capability to participate in and benefit from the digital economy.
Shri Scindia said that if Digital India democratised access, Intelligent India must democratise intelligence. AI cannot remain the preserve of corporates or banks. It must become a tool available to every citizen, enabling each person to benefit from the transformation underway.
The Union Minister highlighted India’s indigenous 4G telecom stack, noting that telecom stacks have historically been developed by a small number of countries and companies. India has now produced its own domestic 4G stack and is working on 5G.
Shri Scindia said India’s 6G mission has already started, with the ambition of contributing 10% of global 6G patents and becoming a valuable partner in the development of 6G standards.
Concluding, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia said India must “Innovate in India, serve in India, serve the world and serve it securely.” He said the ambition must be to move from a connected India to intelligent digital finance and then to empowered finance, and from Digital Public Infrastructure to trusted infrastructure.

Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) issued The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) (Repealing) Regulations, 2026 (4 of 2026) dated 10.09.2026 to repeal the Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) Regulations, 2012 (15 of 2012) dated 14th May 2012, along with all orders and directions issued thereunder, with effect from the date of its notification in the Official Gazette.
The Standards of Quality of Service (Duration of Advertisements in Television Channels) Regulations, 2012 prescribes a ceiling of twelve minutes of advertisements in a clock hour in broadcast of a programme. The regulations empower the Authority to issue order or direction to service providers to protect the interests of the subscribers or for ensuring compliance of the regulations.
These Regulations were primarily intended to monitor and enforce, as a quality-of-service measure, the advertisement duration ceiling prescribed under rule 7, sub-rule (11) of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), vide notification published in the Official Gazette on 21
st
August 2026, omitted sub-rule (11) of rule 7 of the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, thereby removing the twelve-minute advertisement duration cap prescribed for television channels. title: Government amends E-Commerce Rules to strengthen consumer protection and promote transparency
subtitle:
Amended Rules strengthen provisions on consumer grievances, search results, sponsored listings, price reductions, dark patterns and seller disclosures

New Rules to come into force from January 1, 2027
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Consumer Affairs, Government of India, has amended the
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
through the
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026
, with the objective of strengthening consumer protection while facilitating a transparent and balanced regulatory framework for the e-commerce sector.
The amended Rules seek to address emerging consumer concerns in the digital marketplace while taking into account the need for
Ease of Doing Business
and a balanced approach that protects consumer interests without imposing unnecessary regulatory burdens on e-commerce entities.
A key provision of the amended Rules requires
every e-commerce entity to become a partner in the convergence process of the
National Consumer Helpline (NCH)
,
strengthening the integration of e-commerce platforms with the national consumer grievance redressal mechanism.
During 2025, the NCH received
17,71,622 grievances
, of which
5,11,196, or around 29 per cent, related to the e-commerce sector
.
Key Amendments
The amended Rules provide for:
Consumer complaints:
Every e-commerce entity shall provide the complainant with a copy of the complaint as recorded by its grievance officer.
Search results:
E-commerce entities shall not manipulate search results in a manner that misleads users or adversely affects the relevance of results to the user's search query.
Sponsored listings:
Sponsored listings shall be identified through clear and prominent disclosures.
Price reductions:
Where a price reduction is announced, the reduced price and prior price shall both be displayed. The “prior price” means the lowest price at which the goods or services were offered during the 30 days preceding the announcement.
Dark patterns:
E-commerce entities shall comply with the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, undertake a yearly self-audit and prominently display a certificate of compliance.
Seller and product information
: Marketplace e-commerce entities shall provide key information, including best before/use before dates, return/refund, warranty, delivery and payment details, to enable informed consumer decisions.
Consumer information:
Marketplace e-commerce entities shall not use consumer information for specified purposes without express and affirmative consent.
Bundled fees:
Marketplace e-commerce entities shall not collect
bundled fees for services unrelated to the e-commerce platform
, subject to the specified exception for loyalty or membership programmes.
Imported goods:
Importer details and country of origin
shall be disclosed for imported goods.
Strengthening the e-commerce framework
The
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
, notified under the
Consumer Protection Act, 2019
,
provide the framework for safeguarding consumers against unfair trade practices in the e-commerce sector. The amended Rules further strengthen this framework in view of evolving business models, digital practices and consumer expectations.
The amendments seek to establish a
more transparent, accountable and consumer-centric e-commerce ecosystem
, while providing clarity to e-commerce entities on their responsibilities and enabling a level-playing field for businesses operating in the digital marketplace.
The Department of Consumer Affairs remains committed to ensuring that the growth and innovation of India's e-commerce sector is accompanied by
effective consumer protection, transparency, fair business practices and Ease of Doing Business
, while maintaining an appropriate balance between the interests of consumers and e-commerce entities.
The
Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 shall come into force from January 1, 2027.

The investigations revealed the gold capsules had been handed over to him in the transit area by a transit passenger and involvement of another female airport staff. In swift follow up operation two transit passengers were intercepted at Mumbai Airport while they were handing over the five gold capsules to the airport staff. The transit passengers had arrived from Muscat and Dubai for onwards journey to Bangkok after the delivery of the smuggled gold. A female airline staff, for her involvement in clandestine removal of the smuggled gold from the airport along with the recipient of the goods were also apprehended.
In all, 8 capsules containing gold dust in wax form, weighing
3.47 kg
in net weight, were recovered and seized

title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah chairs the third meeting of the Governing Body of the NIDM in New Delhi
subtitle:
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, over the past 12 years, there has been a fundamental transformation in both the approach and the methodology of disaster management

Earlier, disasters were viewed only from the perspective of relief and rehabilitation, today we are advancing into a new era of risk reduction, early warning systems, and Zero Casualty

We have successfully tackled many disasters with Zero Casualty, which is a major achievement

The goal of Modi govt. is to make disaster-resilient villages and disaster-resilient cities, we must move forward by keeping this as a priority

Today, NIDM has become a national centre for research, innovation, and capacity building, new horizons will have to be explored by integrating universities into it

Due to environmental protection, risk reduction, resilience, and a comprehensive national vision, India is gradually emerging as an ideal model in the world

Moving beyond training and guidelines, we should also advance towards a ‘Whole of Government’ approach in building a system to stand firmly against disasters

In the era of global warming, climate change, and new scientific innovations, the relevance and need for both NIDM and NDMA will grow even further in days to come

Mobile application developed for disaster management should be widely promoted and adopted across the higher, secondary, and primary education sectors

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also taken the decision to ensure that the distribution of disaster relief funds is undertaken through a scientific and systematic process

Just as we adopted a ‘Whole of Government’ approach to effectively address disasters, we must move forward with the same approach to further strengthen and institutionalise disaster management

Under the Modi Government, the allocation to SDRF has increased nearly fourfold, while allocation to NDRF has increased nearly threefold

Along with transforming the approach to disaster management, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also laid special emphasis on environmental protection

At one point, NIDM was confined to a corner of Krishi Bhavan, former PM Atal Ji brought it under MHA and gave it a new lease of life, PM Modi further revitalised the institution by facilitating the allocation of land for it, today the transformed and expanded NIDM stands before the nation as a testament to this vision and commitment

All stakeholders should establish a dedicated and focused cell within their respective departments to ensure the effective implementation of these agenda items, the heads of the respective departments should review the progress once every three months and accord the necessary priority to their implementation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today chaired the third meeting of the Governing Body of the National Institute of Disaster Management (NIDM) in New Delhi. The meeting was attended by the Union Home Secretary, Vice-Chancellor of Delhi University, Member and Head of Department of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Director General of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Secretary of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Director General of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Director of the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA), Executive Director of NIDM, and senior officials from several Central Ministries and State Governments.
Addressing the meeting, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi there has been a comprehensive transformation in both the approach and methodology of disaster management over the last 12 years. The Modi Government has completely transformed the entire disaster management system, set the goal of ‘Zero Casualty’ and taken the country towards achieving this objective. We have also successfully faced several disasters with ‘Zero Casualty’, which is a major achievement. Shri Shah said that earlier disasters were viewed only from the perspective of relief and rehabilitation. Today, we have entered a new era based on three pillars - risk reduction, early warning systems and ‘Zero Casualty’. This is a matter of pride for all of us. He said that in this direction, the ‘Whole of Government’ approach is increasingly becoming an integral part of our work culture. Whenever a disaster occurs, all government departments actively respond. Now, with the strength of new research, we should take this process forward with greater speed and ensure continuous monitoring. Just as a ‘Whole of Government’ approach has been adopted in dealing with disasters, we must also move forward with a ‘Whole of Government’ approach to further strengthen the disaster management system.
Union Home Minister said that along with the transformation in the approach to disaster management, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has also laid special emphasis on environmental protection. He said that ultimately environmental protection is the most effective means of preventing disasters. Environmental protection, risk reduction, resilience and a broad national vision are enabling India to gradually emerge as a model for the world. Initiatives such as Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), Pro-Planet People and the International Solar Alliance (ISA) are making an important contribution to disaster prevention. Shri Shah said that the ‘Zero Casualty’ approach should not be applied only at the site of a disaster. Zero Casualty can also be achieved by preventing disasters from occurring in the first place. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has envisioned a safe and balanced world, going beyond the conventional approach of world leaders.
Shri Amit Shah said that there was a time when the predecessor of NIDM, the National Centre for Disaster Management was lying almost inactive in a corner of Krishi Bhawan. However, in 2003, the then Prime Minister Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee took the historic decision to give it a new lease of life. Keeping in view the wide scope of the subject and the need for coordination among various agencies, it was decided to bring the institution under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has played a significant role in revitalizing the institution. NIDM has emerged in its present form with a transformed and strengthened role before the country.
Union Home Minister said that the relevance and significance of both NIDM and NDMA are going to increase further in the coming days. The number of disasters is likely to increase due to global warming and climate change. At the same time, new types of disasters may also emerge due to new applications of science and their expanding areas of use. Keeping all these aspects in mind, the two institutions share responsibilities ranging from policy-making to training and implementation. In some areas, both institutions are also working together.
Shri Amit Shah directed all stakeholders to constitute a dedicated cell in their respective departments for implementation of the agenda. He said that departmental heads should conduct a review meeting of the cell at least once every three months and accord priority to this subject.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that NDMA and NIDM should study research being undertaken across the world in the field of disaster management and make efforts to implement its findings in India in accordance with local requirements. The Department of Agriculture should focus on permanent preparedness to deal with locust swarm attacks originating from the Pakistan side. He said that the best practices being adopted in other countries to deal with such attacks should be implemented in India. Shri Shah added that seriousness should be ensured in disaster management training and priority should be given to those who are genuinely committed to the subject in disaster management training programmes.
Union Home Minister said that NIDM and NDMA should jointly issue guidelines for the entire country. These guidelines should clearly specify what should and should not be done in the event of each type of disaster and how it should be done. NIDM should undertake the training component while the NDRF, State Disaster Response Forces (SDRFs) and other concerned agencies should work together to implement these guidelines on the ground.
Shri Amit Shah said that it is extremely important to prepare a document, through research, identifying the causes of disasters. Effective prevention and rescue measures can be developed on this basis. After every disaster, a joint team of NDMA and NIDM should be constituted, including the NDRF and SDRF. These four institutions should jointly study the causes of the damage and prepare a detailed report.
Shri Amit Shah said that NIDM has emerged as a national centre for research, innovation, policy support, training and departmental cooperation. We need to further strengthen these four pillars and explore new horizons. There are still unexplored areas in research, innovation, training, policy support and departmental cooperation that we should seek to address in the coming days. He said that NIDM has already taken steps in this direction. There is a need to take knowledge and best practices beyond departmental silos. In the coming days we must develop the habit of working in a coordinated manner, rising above departmental boundaries.
Union Home Minister said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has decided that the distribution of disaster funds should also be carried out through a scientific process. The allocation under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) has increased nearly fourfold, while the allocation under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) has increased nearly threefold. Around ₹2.5 lakh crore has been spent in this sector over the last 11 years, which is a major achievement. The Disaster Management Act was amended after 20 years. The concept of Urban Disaster Management Authorities was introduced and such authorities have also been established. The process of creating digital disaster databases at the national and state levels has begun. The National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC) has been accorded statutory status. In addition, the 16th Finance Commission has provided for ₹2 lakh crore for this period.
Shri Amit Shah said that the mobile application that has been developed needs to be widely promoted through primary, secondary and higher education. The Government is making every possible effort to strengthen NIDM. Recently, four acres of land have also been allocated for the institution. NIDM is working towards developing itself as a world-class model institution, and both its campuses are functioning smoothly. Shri Shah said that while enhancing international cooperation is undoubtedly commendable, our priority must continue to focus on the five lakh villages of the country. Keeping this priority in mind, there should be no objection to learning as much as possible from the world and enabling the world to learn as much as possible from us. He stated that the Modi government's goal is to create disaster-resilient villages and cities, and we must move forward by prioritizing this objective.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that a provision should be made for at least one top-level meeting of NIDM to be held every year so that the meetings are meaningful and outcome-oriented and effective implementation of the decisions taken is ensured. He said that through this institution, we must transform knowledge into capacity, capacity into preparedness and preparedness into outcomes, so that together we can achieve the goal of ‘Zero Casualty’.

content:
Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, today chaired a high-level meeting with State Urban Development Ministers, Principal Secretaries, Urban Development and State Mission Directors to review the preparedness of States and Union Territories for Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026.
The meeting reviewed preparations for the nationwide campaign, which will be observed from 17th September to 17th October 2026.
This year’s theme, ‘Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’,
underlines the role of collective participation and shared responsibility in advancing the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat.
The key focus areas of SHS 2026
include transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs)
and high-footfall public places; Swachh Paathshala -Yuva for Swachhata; SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivirs; Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata; and Swachhata se Samriddhi, with a focus on circular economy and Waste-to-Wealth initiatives.
During the meeting, States/UTs were briefed on the key focus areas of the campaign and the need to undertake coordinated action across the nation. Emphasis was laid on ensuring extensive citizen participation, effective implementation at the local level and visible cleanliness outcomes during the campaign period. States Departments should take a lead in ensuring cleanliness drives across each office premises, tourist spots and water bodies.
In his remarks, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal,
called upon Citizens to begin the Swachchata hi Seva campaign from their
own homes on 17th September
. He urged
citizens to clean their homes themselves, and thereafter light a Diya in their homes
in the evening, symbolising a clean home, healthy family and positive energy; while also representing a commitment to sustain the cleanliness achieved.  He said that the campaign should be taken forward in the spirit of
‘Seva Sankalp’
, with the objective of making cleanliness a sustained people-led commitment rather than a month-long activity.
Referring to the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Union Minister said that the
campaign begins on 17 September
, the Prime Minister’s birthday, and seeks to connect his spirit of service and resolve with the cause of cleanliness.
Recalling the Prime Minister’s message in Mann Ki Baat, Shri Manohar Lal said that when keeping a place clean becomes the resolve of its people, the change goes beyond cleanliness and transforms the very identity of that place. He emphasised that the endeavour should therefore be to make Swachhata a collective resolve of citizens.
The Minister emphasized that
25th September
, the birthday of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya, should mark cleanliness drives across all segments of society, with particular focus on inclusivity and social welfare.
In particular, States were urged to undertake extensive planning and advocacy activities leading up to
1st October, for nation-wide Shramdaan for
Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath
, where State Education and Sports Departments were asked to engage youth and sportspersons for Swachchata activities at scale. The Minister appealed to all Ministers, MPs/MLAs, Mayors, Deputy Mayors, Ward Councillors, Commissioners, Eminent personalities of each State to lead this nation-wide Shramdaan from their respective areas/constituencies and ensure mass mobilisation for the same.
He also urged all municipalities to engage Residential Societies and RWAs by organising inter-ward and inter- RWA Swachchata Competitions to further bolster their efforts, and promote key Swachchata messaging in prominent RWA locations.
On
2nd October, or Swachch Bharat Diwas
, Special Council meetings and special cleanliness drives would be organised by the ULBs at Public places to share the message of Mahatma Gandhi, and conduct advocacy drives on Solid Waste Management Rules. In addition, tree plantation activities would be conducted under ‘Ek Ped Maa ke Naam’.
The meeting also highlighted the importance of ensuring the welfare, safety and recognition of sanitation workers through
SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivirs
, including linkages with eligible welfare schemes, preventive health check-ups and provision of safety gear. It was emphasized that these Shivirs be organised recurrently across the year for maximum impact.
The Minister further urged States to organise Special Swachchata Programmes on
7th October
, to mark the completion of Hon’ble PM’s 25 years of Public Service.
States/UTs were also advised to undertake effective and innovative advocacy and outreach  with Jan Bhaagidaari, sports events, playing spiritual/soulful songs and Swachchata Anthems, around SHS 2026 and ensure regular reporting of activities undertaken during the campaign; and take pro-active measures to ensure that the Campaign translates to measurable outcomes on the ground and strong behaviour change in every citizen of the Nation. While the campaign officially ends on 17Th October, States were urged to carry the Swachchata momentum forward throughout the year.

The Conference will be attended by Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for Labour & Employment and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Labour Ministers and senior officials from States/UTs, Chairpersons and Secretaries of BOCW Welfare Boards and senior officers from Central and State governments.
The Conference will also review progress on three major initiatives launched at the National Labour Conference held in New Delhi in November 2025, namely the State BOCW Digital Labour Chowk, Labour Chowk-cum-Facilitation Centres and Online BOCW Cess Collection Portal. date:

content:
Minister of State for the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, inaugurated the Technology Centre (TC) at Devanahalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka, on 10 September 2026. The inauguration ceremony was graced by senior officers from the Ministry of MSME, Government of India; Government of Karnataka and representatives from industry and other local stakeholders. The inauguration ceremony also featured an exhibition showcasing the contribution of Indian MSMEs to the Aerospace & ESDM Sectors.
The Ministry of MSME operates a Nation-wide network of Technology Centres (TCs) to foster an enabling environment for MSMEs which will enhance their technological capabilities and competitiveness. Over the years, these Centres have contributed significantly in technology development, industry-grade training, design, prototyping, testing & production support to MSMEs.
The Minister of State for MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, conveyed her best wishes on the inauguration of the Technology Centre (TC), Bengaluru, and welcomed students, industry associations and other stakeholders to the new centre.
She said, “The centre will serve as a hub for training, manufacturing and nurturing young talent. The network of Technology Centres run by the Ministry of MSME are playing an important role in developing young minds and providing them with industry-oriented skills.” She also announced that the next Technology Centre is coming up in Belagaum, Karnataka at a cost of ₹178 crore.
Emphasising the importance of entrepreneurship, the Minister encouraged students and young innovators to pursue startups and contribute to the country’s growth. She said the Ministry is focused on enabling students to study, train and develop their skills to contribute towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.
She further noted that after agriculture, the MSME sector is a major contributor to the Indian economy and stressed the need to further strengthen its contribution to the nation’s growth.
Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME, Government of India, highlighted the recent amendments to the MSMED Act, 2026 to further benefit the MSMEs. He highlighted the significance of TC Bengaluru as a major initiative for nurturing talent and building industry-ready skills. The centre is expected to train around 10,000 trainees every year, providing them with advanced technical skills and opportunities to contribute to the growth of the MSME sector.
Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary and Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, outlined the growth in MSME sector. With over 9.4 crore registered MSMEs contributing 31% to the Indian economy and generating employment of over 41.6 crore, he described MSMEs as the engines of growth. He highlighted the measures taken to facilitate access to finance and access to technology for MSMEs. The Technology Centre at Bengaluru is the latest addition to the network of TCs established by Ministry of MSME across India.
He highlighted the significant progress made by the Ministry in recent years, including initiatives such as TReDS, the Credit Guarantee Scheme, and various other programmes aimed at strengthening the MSME sector.
He also explained the contribution of Technology Centres across India in providing technological, production and advisory support to MSMEs and providing industry-oriented training to the youth.
The TC Bengaluru has been developed by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India with an investment of ₹156 crore on a 10-acre land parcel provided by the Government of Karnataka. Focus Sector of the centre is Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM). The Centre being equipped with state-of-the-art machines and labs, will provide MSMEs access to advanced technologies such as Surface-Mount Technology (SMT) Line, additive manufacturing, CNC 5 Axis and 3 Axis machines, Electric Discharge Machine (EDM), etc.
Dr Rajneesh mentioned that the Technology Centre, Bengaluru, will serve as a key institution for strengthening the MSME ecosystem in the electronics and aerospace sectors by offering advanced design, prototyping, production, training, and consultancy services. The Centre will play an important role in providing state of the art technology support in to MSMEs in electronics and system design manufacturing (ESDM). It will help generating employment, nurturing skilled talent, and promoting sustainable livelihoods not only in Karnataka but also to MSMEs across India.

He said renewable energy has emerged as a powerful instrument of energy security, economic growth, technological progress and employment generation.
The Minister highlighted that India has crossed the milestone of 300 GW of installed non-fossil-fuel capacity. He said the strength of India’s energy transition lies in building a diverse, balanced and resilient energy portfolio suited to the country’s geography, resources and development needs.
Shri Naik emphasised the significant potential of Small Hydro Power in this context. He said India’s presently assessed Small Hydro Power potential is around 21 GW across more than 7,100 identified sites, of which only about 5.2 GW has been harnessed. He noted that this represents a significant opportunity for further development of the sector.
Shri Naik said the significance of Small Hydro Power goes beyond adding generating capacity. He noted that, wherever technically and environmentally feasible, appropriately designed run-of-river projects can provide a renewable energy option requiring relatively less land and avoiding the large-scale submergence and displacement associated with major reservoir-based projects.
He said Small Hydro Power can provide dependable renewable electricity closer to the point of consumption, strengthen decentralised generation and contribute to the resilience of the power system, particularly in geographically challenging regions. The sector can also create employment, support local enterprises and generate economic opportunities in remote areas while maintaining sensitivity towards ecology and local communities.
The Minister highlighted the Government’s proposed Small Hydro Power Development Scheme for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, with an outlay of ₹2,584.60 crore and a target of approximately 1,500 MW of new Small Hydro Power capacity. The Scheme will also incentivise States to prepare Detailed Project Reports for about 200 projects, thereby creating a pipeline of Small Hydro Power projects for future development.
The Minister stressed that Government support alone cannot unlock the full potential of the sector and called for a strong partnership among the Central Government, State Governments, developers, financial institutions, technology providers and investors. He emphasised the need for policy certainty, streamlined approvals, improved ease of doing business, stronger Centre-State coordination and better bankability of projects.
Shri Naik said that the Curtain Raiser Programme marks the beginning of an important national conversation on how India can make fuller and smarter use of its Small Hydro Power potential. He said the dedicated Small Hydro Power session at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026, to be held from 2nd to 5th November 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, will provide an important platform to deliberate on policy reforms, investment, financing, technology and partnerships.
The Minister invited all stakeholders to participate in this national endeavour and work together to harness India’s river systems, geographical diversity, indigenous technological capabilities and modern innovation to build a cleaner, stronger, more self-reliant and sustainable India.
Shri Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), extended a warm invitation to participate in large numbers in the forthcoming Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026.
The Secretary highlighted the long lead time in starting hydropower projects as a key challenge, noting that delays in obtaining forest, environment and right-of-way clearances adversely impact timely project execution. He said that while the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has been assured by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) of timely clearances, particularly for small hydropower projects, a mechanism should be developed to generate and escalate alerts in cases of undue delays.
Emphasising the need to improve the bankability of small hydropower projects, the Secretary said that their unique cash-flow profile necessitates access to long-term patient capital. He urged the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) to take the lead in working with banks and multilateral development institutions, including the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the World Bank, to facilitate greater availability of patient capital for project developers.
He urged the stakeholders to share their ideas and experiences and suggest what else could be done to promote hydropower, particularly small hydropower, in the country.
Several stakeholders, along with senior officials, delegates from research and industry sectors, were present during the Curtain Raiser.
