title: Fueling the Blue Economy
subtitle: Six Years of Empowering India’s Fisheries Sector under PMMSY
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 SEP 2026 12:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) has strengthened India’s fisheries sector. The Government allocated a record
₹
2,500 crore
in BE 2026
–
27 under PMMSY, reaffirming its commitment to the sector. Fish production increased from
141.64 lakh tonnes
in 2019-20 to a record
197.75 lakh tonnes
in 2024-25. Fisheries exports rose from
₹
46,663 crore in 2019
–
20 to
₹
73,890 crore
in 2025
–
26, reflecting strong sectoral growth. The scheme created employment opportunities for
58 lakh persons
in fisheries and aquaculture-related activities. It also approved
₹
2,797 crore
for cold-chain and marketing infrastructure, strengthening post-harvest management and market connectivity.
A
dditionally,
2,195 FFPOs
were supported through projects worth
₹
544.86 crore
, strengthening collective empowerment.
Strengthening India’s Blue Economy
India's fisheries sector is a vital economic pillar,
sustaining nearly three crore livelihoods
, especially among marginalised and coastal communities. As a recognised
Sunrise Sector
, it has seen consistent growth driven by policies that boost production, exports, infrastructure, and technology adoption. To further unlock this potential, the Government introduced the
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY),
focused on fostering inclusive and sustainable growth across the sector. As PMMSY completes
six years on 10 September 2026
, it stands as a landmark in the transformation of the Indian fisheries sector towards modernisation, sustainability, and prosperity. Since its launch in 2020, the scheme has built stronger infrastructure, opened up new opportunities, and provided consistent support to fishers and fish farmers across the country.
Building on the
Blue Revolution scheme
, PMMSY was conceived to address critical gaps across the fisheries value chain.
The Government has been implementing PMMSY since 2020–21, with a total outlay of
₹
20,750 crore
.
The Government reaffirmed its commitment by allocating a
record
₹
2,500 crore in BE 2026
–
27 under PMMSY
, strengthening fisheries infrastructure and livelihoods.
The scheme has also continued to support large-scale investments in fisheries and aquaculture infrastructure.
As of 11th August 2026
, during the period
2020–21 to 2025–26
, the Department of Fisheries has approved fisheries and aquaculture projects worth
₹
21,394.88 crore
, including a
Central share of ₹
9,510.89 crore
. These approvals, based on proposals received from
States, Union Territories and various implementing agencies
, are supporting infrastructure development and strengthening the fisheries value chain across the country.
PMMSY has focused on transforming India’s fisheries sector
by enhancing production and productivity, modernising the value chain, generating livelihood opportunities, increasing incomes, boosting exports and GVA, strengthening fishers’ security and welfare, and improving fisheries management and regulation.
Success Story: From Ice Plant to Greater Prosperity
In Porbandar, Gujarat, Mr. Pravinbhai Babulal Masani has spent over two decades building his fishing enterprise.
With extensive experience in the industry, he understood that investing in a new ice plant could strengthen his business. However, the high cost of establishing an ice plant was beyond his financial capacity. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) provided him with an opportunity through financial assistance for establishing ice plants.
In 2021–22, Mr. Masani successfully received
a
₹
48 lakh subsidy
under PMMSY. With this support, he established a
30 MT/day ice plant
, enabling him to produce high-quality ice blocks for fishing boats. The new facility helps fishing boats carry sufficient ice to keep fish fresh and reduce spoilage during fishing operations. This has strengthened Mr. Masani’s fishing business, improved his earnings, and supported a better livelihood for his family. His journey demonstrates how targeted support under PMMSY can help fishers invest in essential infrastructure, strengthen their businesses, and contribute to fisheries growth.
Transforming India’s Fisheries Sector through PMMSY
The PMMSY is an umbrella scheme comprising Central Sector (CS) and Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) components.
Central Sector (CS):
Fully funded and implemented by the Central Government.
The Central Sector component supports genetic improvement, innovation, technology demonstrations, training, aquatic quarantine, harbour modernisation, disease surveillance and fisheries data systems. It also strengthens the National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) and fisheries institutions, fisher safety, FFPOs, cooperatives and SHGs, while promoting certification, traceability, accreditation and labelling. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) is a Central Sector sub-scheme. It operates under the broader ambit of PMMSY. The scheme complements and reinforces PMMSY's overarching objectives. Its specific mandate is to strengthen the development of the fisheries sector.
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY)
The
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY)
is a Central Sector sub-scheme implemented under the umbrella of the
PMMSY
. Operational across all States and Union Territories for four years from 2023-24 to 2026-27, it carries an estimated financial outlay of
₹
6,000 crore.
The scheme facilitates the structural transformation of the fisheries sector by advancing formalisation,
expanding insurance coverage, strengthening access to institutional finance, and promoting quality assurance
and
traceability
across the fisheries value chain. It aims to enhance financial resilience, risk mitigation, and market integration for fishers, aquaculture farmers, and allied stakeholders, thereby fostering a more organised, transparent, and sustainable fisheries sector.
Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS):
Partially funded by the Central Government and implemented by States and Union Territories. CSS activities include:
Enhancement of Fish Production and Productivity
: Focuses on increasing fish production and productivity through
technology infusion and improved fisheries practices
. It covers
inland fisheries, marine fisheries, mariculture, seaweed cultivation, development of fisheries in Himalayan and North-Eastern States/UTs, and ornamental fisheries
.
Infrastructure and Post-Harvest Management:
Strengthens fisheries infrastructure through
fishing harbours, fish landing centres and post-harvest facilities
.
It also supports
cold-chain infrastructure, deep-sea fishing, integrated modern coastal fishing villages, markets and marketing infrastructure
.
Fisheries Management and Regulatory Framework
:
Promotes
monitoring, control and surveillance
,
insurance for fishing vessels and fishers, and fisheries extension and support services. It also strengthens the
safety and security of fishers at sea
while supporting the
livelihood and nutritional needs of fishers.
PMMSY: Strengthening Production, Infrastructure and Livelihoods

Technology-Driven Aquaculture
The scheme promotes technology-driven aquaculture systems that enhance productivity while optimising land and water use. It supports high-density, water-efficient models such as Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Bio-floc technology, improving output, water quality, resource efficiency and environmental sustainability.
Recirculatory Aquaculture System (RAS)
: RAS filters and recirculates water, removing waste and impurities while enabling intensive fish farming with minimal land and water.
Bio-floc Technology:
It is a sustainable aquaculture method that recycles nutrients in water using beneficial microbes. These microbes form clumps called bio-floc, which serve as natural feed and also help clean the water. This method requires little or no water exchange, making it ideal for high-density fish farming with minimal resources. It boosts productivity while being environmentally friendly, earning it the name “green soup” or heterotrophic ponds in aquaculture circles.
Digital Transformation of Fisheries
Beyond modernising production systems, PMMSY is also driving the digital transformation of the fisheries sector. The
National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP)
was launched under PM-MKSSY in September 2024. It aims to advance digital governance and formalisation in the fisheries and aquaculture sector. The NFDP creates work-based digital identities and a comprehensive stakeholder database to formalise the sector. Operationally, it functions as a single-window digital system, enabling beneficiaries to access institutional credit, aquaculture insurance, traceability mechanisms, and performance-linked incentives. The platform also supports fisheries cooperatives, training, and capacity-building initiatives. As of 8 September 2026, the NFDP platform has recorded over
37.01 lakh
individual registrations, with total registrations crossing
37.23 lakh
.
Contribution to SDG 14: Life Below Water
PMMSY promotes sustainable and responsible fisheries and aquaculture, supporting the sustainable use of aquatic resources. The scheme also promotes sustainable fish production methods and modern aquaculture practices, including Bio-floc, RAS, cage culture and mariculture. These interventions contribute to SDG 14 (Life Below Water) by supporting sustainable management of fisheries and aquaculture and strengthening aquatic resource conservation.
Towards Sustainable Fisheries and Blue Economy Growth
The fisheries sector occupies an important place in India’s agricultural and rural economy, contributing to livelihoods, food security, employment and exports. The
Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
is driving the transformation of India’s fisheries sector by strengthening production, infrastructure, technology, livelihoods and sustainability. Its investments in modern infrastructure, cold-chain facilities, technology-driven aquaculture and digital platforms are strengthening the fisheries value chain. Continued support for fishers, fish farmers and coastal communities can create opportunities for higher incomes and improved market access. These efforts also contribute to Sustainable Development Goal 14 (Life Below Water) by promoting sustainable use and conservation of aquatic resources. With sustained investments, PMMSY has laid the foundation for a modern, competitive and sustainable fisheries sector. As India advances its Blue Economy vision, PMMSY will continue to play a pivotal role in enhancing livelihoods, strengthening food security, boosting exports and promoting responsible utilisation of aquatic resources.
